name: Hosea
bio:
Hosea son of Beeri prophesied to Israel during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah in Judah and Jeroboam II in Israel. At the LORD's command, he married Gomer, a woman who would be unfaithful to him, as a living picture of Israel's unfaithfulness to God; he named their children Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah ("not pitied"), and Lo-ammi ("not my people") as symbolic warnings of coming judgment (Hosea 1:1-2:1).

When Gomer left him for other lovers, the LORD told Hosea to buy her back for fifteen shekels of silver and some barley and take her home again, requiring her to live faithfully with him without other men — a dramatic reenactment of God's persistent love for an unfaithful Israel, who would eventually return to seek the LORD and "David their king" in the latter days (Hosea 3:1-5). The rest of his book, delivered mostly in direct prophetic oracles rather than narrative, condemns Israel's idolatry and alliances with foreign powers while promising eventual restoration and healing for those who return to God.
